title: Deep Space Chroma · birefringence

reference.grammar: photoelastic fringes: a retardation field seen through a plane polariscope with a warm source; isoclinic wedges through the focus; soft focus; mono grain
reference.set: 21 plates, 5000 × 3500, ø co. “Deep Space Chroma” key visuals

units: normalized by width: x ∈ [0,1], y ∈ [0, H/W]; δ in nm; angles in degrees, screen space (y down)

physics.transmission: I(λ) = S(λ) · sin²(2(ψ − β)) · sin²(π δ / λ) for a crossed plane polariscope; the first sin² is the isoclinic term (achromatic), the second the isochromatic term (chromatic)
physics.stress_optic: δ = C · t · (σ1 − σ2) — retardation is proportional to the principal stress difference
physics.color: XYZ = ∫ I(λ) [x̄ ȳ z̄](λ) dλ over 380–720 nm at 4 nm; XYZ → linear sRGB
physics.chart: the Michel-Lévy chart is color(δ) for δ = 0…1600 nm; it is computed at load, not hand-drawn

palette.derived: from the chart — nothing is hand-picked

techniques.name: Spectral Michel-Lévy chart

params.source: Planck 3000 K, green dip .1 at 548 ± 48 nm
params.integration: 380–720 nm, 4 nm steps, Wyman–Sloan–Shirley CMF fit

techniques.implementation: For every δ from 0 to 1599 nm the transmitted spectrum sin²(πδ/λ)·S(λ) is integrated against the color-matching functions; the 1600 colors are the LUT the field is shaded with. Order 1 (0–560 nm) is where the plates live: black → grey → warm white → amber → orange → red; the mauve and blue of 560–700 are the cool lanes.

techniques.name: Retardation field

params.sheet: δ = (d0 + A · sign(c)|c|^shape) · (1 + pin/r), c = cos(k · θw + ph + flow · t); shape for the peaks (blue), shapeN for the dips (pale) — the pale lanes are the narrow ones
params.radial: + rad · r — orange near the focus, red far out
params.load: δ = K · |σ1 − σ2| from Σ Flamant point loads (σr = −2F cos(θ−α)/(π r^decay)) + a uniform stress
params.biaxial: δ = d0 + c · |p − A| · |p − B| (Cassini ovals)
params.ribbon: δ = d0 + A · tanh(d / period) — a ramp across the ribbon: white, orange, red, blue in order
params.ring: δ = d0 + A · tanh((r − R) / period)

techniques.implementation: Each family is one expression for δ. The sheet keeps δ in the orange-red most of the time (shape 2.4 dwells near d0) and dips to white or peaks to blue briefly; the load family is real plane-stress mechanics; the conoscopes are the textbook interference figures.

techniques.name: Slow-axis field ψ

params.domain_warp: (x, y) += wa · noise2((x, y) · wf), 2-octave value noise, wa .1 W, wf 1.2; the same hash in JS and GLSL
params.sheet: ψ = θw + twist · r + spiral · ln r
params.load: ψ = ½ · atan2(2τ, σx − σy) (principal direction)

techniques.implementation: ψ decides where the isoclinics fall. The domain warp bends the sheet — the plates are not flat starbursts — and warping θ makes lanes of unequal width; neither breaks the physics because δ and ψ are still evaluated from one coordinate.

techniques.name: Isoclinics

params.term: sin²(m · (ψ − β + skew · sin(ψ − β)))^sharp, sharp for the β arm and sharp2 for the β + 180° arm
params.circular: circ mixes toward 1 (a circular polariscope removes isoclinics)
params.note: m = 2 is the physical crossed-polar cross (four arms); the plates read as two arms, m = 1, one polarizer effective

techniques.implementation: Multiplies the whole image; the black wedges are not masks but extinction where the material axis is parallel to the polarizer. Spinning β sweeps them around the focus.

techniques.name: Envelope
techniques.implementation: mix(floor, chart(δ) · iso, env): the load point is opaque, the far field sinks, nothing reaches 0.

techniques.name: Plate look (camera + grade)

params.hue_grade: after gamma, hues pulled .75 of the way toward 6° (warm) or 196° (cool), whichever is nearer; saturation × 1.4 first
params.bloom: highlights (brightness .8, contrast 2.5 → a threshold near L .4) blurred at σ .05 W and added at .4 — the glow along the hot edges
params.shoulder: x/(1 + .25x), then highlights above L .6 desaturate .85 toward a pink-white
params.measured: plates carry no yellow, no green, no magenta — the grade explains the absence; band means: (235,182,147) (232,143,94) (225,95,57) (185,53,40) red side, (165,196,199) (120,154,165) (79,105,116) blue side, white (222,190,184)

techniques.implementation: Applied to the chart once (1600 entries), so per-pixel cost is a lookup; this is the step that turns a textbook chart into the plate palette.

techniques.name: Post defocus

params.measured: p99 horizontal gradient 12/255 per px at 1600 px

techniques.implementation: One gaussian over the finished color image; blurring after the chart is what mixes neighboring lanes into the grey-mauve transitions.

techniques.name: Mono grain
techniques.implementation: Multiplicative hashed noise, identical across channels.

techniques.name: Polariscope motion
techniques.implementation: Every motion is a physical control of the instrument: rotate the polarizer, load the sheet, turn the sheet.

pass_order: chart · integrate the spectrum once → color(δ)
field · δ(x,y) and ψ(x,y) for the family
envelope · pinch × vignette × lobe gain, mix from the floor
bloom · thresholded highlights, σ .05 W, add .4
notes: The chart parameters were tuned by eye against the 21 plates; the field parameters against plate 09 (focus (0.47, 0.345 W), a wide isoclinic arm straight up and a narrower one straight down).
Motion is CPU on a 400 px work canvas in the plate; engine.html is the GPU version.
engine.html carries a first-pass preset for every plate (by eye) — refine with the sliders, Copy JSON.
